players.product: 1.6T PAM4 DSP, TIAs, drivers, silicon photonics light engines, coherent DSP, custom XPU silicon

quarterly_data.signal: Q4 FY2026 results: record revenue of $2.219 billion, up 22% year-over-year and 7% sequentially, above the guidance midpoint on data center demand; data center revenue a record $1.65 billion (9% sequential, 21% year-over-year growth, 74% of total revenue) with sequential growth across optical interconnects, custom silicon, switching and storage; non-GAAP gross margin 59%, non-GAAP operating margin 35.7%, non-GAAP EPS $0.80. Fiscal 2026 revenue $8.195 billion, up 42%. Q4 inventory $1.39 billion (up $374 million QoQ to support growth), total debt $4.47 billion (gross debt-to-EBITDA 1.38x); $2.245 billion returned to stockholders in fiscal 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: $2.219 billion Q4 revenue (22% YoY, 7% sequential); data center $1.65 billion (21% YoY, 74% of revenue); FY2026 revenue $8.195 billion (42%); inventory $1.39 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance and FY2027 outlook: Q1 FY2027 revenue $2.4 billion plus or minus 5% (8% sequential growth at the midpoint, 27% year-over-year), non-GAAP gross margin 58.25% to 59.25%, non-GAAP EPS $0.74 to $0.84; data center to grow approximately 10% sequentially in Q1. Management expects revenue to grow every quarter at a similar sequential rate, exiting FY2027 with Q4 revenue exceeding $3 billion, and FY2027 revenue to grow more than 30% to approaching $11 billion (up from approximately $9.5 billion given in September 2025 and approximately $10 billion in December 2025), entirely driven by data center, which is now seen growing 40%. Interconnect is now expected to grow more than 50% versus a prior expectation of 30%; communications and other to grow 10%. Celestial AI and XConn add approximately $75 million to FY2027 non-GAAP opex and are not expected to contribute meaningful revenue until fiscal 2028. Bookings are 'accelerating at a record pace'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 FY2027 revenue $2.4 billion (plus or minus 5%); FY2027 approaching $11 billion (more than 30%); Q4 FY2027 exceeding $3 billion; data center 40%; interconnect more than 50% (prior 30%)

quarterly_data.signal: FY2028 outlook: total revenue to grow close to 40% to approximately $15 billion, roughly $2 billion higher than the December outlook, with non-GAAP EPS 'well over $5'; data center revenue to grow close to 50%, driven by interconnect significantly outpacing cloud CapEx growth, custom at least doubling and Ethernet switching ramping; Celestial AI and XConn to contribute approximately $250 million in aggregate revenue; communications to grow low single digits. Murphy said the outlook rests on 'extremely strong bookings and backlog' and detailed supply-planning conversations with customers, and that Marvell is on track to the calendar 2028 targets set in April 2024.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2028 revenue approximately $15 billion (close to 40%); data center close to 50%; Celestial AI + XConn approximately $250 million; non-GAAP EPS well over $5

quarterly_data.signal: Scale-out PAM: 800-gig demand remains robust and 800 will still be the majority of volume in FY2027, while very strong bookings from multiple Tier 1 customers for 1.6T (in production since the second half of fiscal 2026, with significant shipments at the end of last year) drive a very rapid 1.6T ramp in FY2027 and substantial additional growth in FY2028. Marvell was first to productize 200-gigabit per lane and has demonstrated 400-gig per lane technology for the later 3.2T transition. Murphy said the electro-optics business is now growing '50% plus' this year, tracking accelerator growth rather than CapEx, helped by a rising optics attach rate on new XPU/GPU generations and the higher ASP of 1.6T.
quarterly_data.figure: 1.6T in production since second half of fiscal 2026; electro-optics growing 50% plus in FY2027; 400-gig per lane demonstrated for 3.2T

quarterly_data.signal: Scale-across and campus: Marvell leads DCI with Coherent 400-gig and 800-gig modules and expects to supply DCI modules to all five major U.S. hyperscalers this year; industry forecasts see the DCI pluggable TAM growing by more than 5x by calendar 2030. Announced the industry's first Secure 1.6T ZR and ZR+ DCI modules on a new 2-nanometer Coherent DSP plus a 2-nanometer 800-gig DSP, sampling later this year. First-generation 1.6T Coherent light products (2 to 20-kilometer campus reach) are shipping, with a second generation adding integrated MACsec.
quarterly_data.figure: DCI modules to all five major U.S. hyperscalers this year; DCI pluggable TAM more than 5x by calendar 2030; 2-nanometer 1.6T ZR/ZR+ DSP sampling later this year

quarterly_data.signal: Scale-up CPO: the Celestial AI and XConn acquisitions have closed. Celestial AI's photonic fabric chiplets are to be co-packaged into custom XPUs and scale-up switches, enabling large-scale CPO deployment for scale-up starting next year; the first-generation chiplet is being brought into high-volume manufacturing. Celestial CPO revenue remains on track for a $500 million annualized run rate in Q4 fiscal 2028, doubling to a $1 billion annualized run rate by Q4 fiscal 2029; the scale-up interconnect market could exceed $10 billion by 2030. Murphy: 'we'll be shipping next year CPO for scale up at one large customer', with the rest of scale-up deployments still copper-based, and CPO in scale-out expected to stay relatively limited versus pluggables.
quarterly_data.figure: $500 million annualized run rate in Q4 fiscal 2028; $1 billion annualized run rate by Q4 fiscal 2029; scale-up interconnect market could exceed $10 billion by 2030

quarterly_data.signal: AEC and retimers: design wins with 3 Tier 1 U.S. hyperscalers plus model builders and hardware OEMs; combined AEC and retimer revenue expected to more than double year-over-year in FY2027; asked for the base, Murphy said 'it's doubling -- over doubling this year, but it's probably in the $200 million range', adding 'maybe that goes higher'. Marvell entered when retimers and AECs moved from NRZ to PAM and runs a Golden Cable program giving hyperscalers multiple cable OEMs on the same Marvell DSP reference design.
quarterly_data.figure: AEC + retimer revenue more than double in FY2027; 'probably in the $200 million range'; design wins with 3 Tier 1 U.S. hyperscalers

quarterly_data.signal: Switching: data center switch revenue exceeded $300 million in fiscal 2026, all scale-out, and is now expected to surpass $600 million in FY2027 (up from $500 million indicated last quarter) on 12.8T demand and the 51.2T ramp; the 100T switch is expected to begin sampling in the first half of the fiscal year. In scale-up, XConn adds PCIe/CXL switching (PCIe Gen 6 and CXL 3.1 monolithic switch supporting up to 256 lanes; engaged with more than 20 customers before the deal); UALink 115T solutions to sample in the second half of FY2027 with volume production in fiscal 2028, and Celestial CPO can be integrated directly with Marvell switches.
quarterly_data.figure: switch revenue exceeding $300 million FY2026; surpass $600 million FY2027 (prior $500 million); UALink 115T sampling second half, volume fiscal 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Custom business: grown from zero to $1.5 billion in fiscal 2026, doubling year-over-year in the first full production year. FY2027 custom revenue expected to grow more than 20% (Murphy: 'biased upwards'), with a stronger second half as the lead XPU program transitions to its next generation, for which Marvell holds purchase orders covering the entire fiscal year's forecast and is ramping production; Marvell is also engaged on the follow-on generation. FY2028 custom revenue expected to at least double, driven by existing programs, XPU-attach (custom NIC and CXL) reaching high volume, and a new Tier 1 XPU program with firm volume requirements for all of next year; Murphy said the plug for the new program is 'significantly lower than actually the wafers that we're planning on starting'. Marvell cites 20-plus design wins in or going into production an unprecedented level of activity across multiple new engagements, and a massive opportunity on 2-nanometer and below process technologies.
quarterly_data.figure: custom revenue $1.5 billion FY2026; more than 20% growth FY2027; at least double FY2028; 20-plus design wins

quarterly_data.signal: XPU attach: several programs ramp in FY2027, including initial CXL and NIC products; CXL demand is accelerating partly on tight memory supply, since custom CXL expanders let customers reuse prior-generation DRAM. Line of sight to revenue exceeding $2 billion by fiscal 2029 from custom NIC and CXL alone. Murphy sized XPU attach at roughly a couple of hundred million last year, doubling this year and perhaps more than doubling again, 'probably a $1 billion type business' by next year, against an XPU attach TAM of about $15 billion in calendar '28 where Marvell targets about 20% share (about $3 billion).
quarterly_data.figure: NIC + CXL revenue exceeding $2 billion by fiscal 2029; XPU attach a $1 billion type business by next year; XPU attach TAM about $15 billion in calendar '28

quarterly_data.signal: Supply: COO Chris Koopmans said supply has been tight 'for anything that touches AI, advanced node wafer fabrication, advanced packaging, large body substrate since the launch of ChatGPT', yet Marvell grew north of 40% last year by giving suppliers multiple years of visibility, and he is very confident Marvell has secured the supply needed for the outlined growth this year, next year and beyond.
